title: Finite reduction comparison of the ordinary projection arrow
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l. For arbitrary schemes X,Y, a morphism f:X→Y with a supplied compactification c, three representative-normalized tensor models over the completed integral coefficient sheaves on X,c.Z,Y [def-pur-integral-compact-support-coefficient-data], arbitrary unbounded completed-coefficient complexes K,L, and every n≥0, there is an isomorphism in the arrow category between the nth scalar reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] of the ordinary proper-counit/open-extension projection [def-exchange-projection] and the canonical constant-scalar realization of the fixed-scalar finite compactification projection at the inverse realizations of the nth reductions of K,L. The finite ring is O_E/(varpi_E^(n+1)). No constructibility, completeness, field-base hypotheses or invertibility of either projection are asserted.

source.place: Proper projection paragraph: reduction of the actual canonical projection is the torsion projection map; pasted with the open projection of def-exchange-projection.

proof.text: The positive quotient of the completed coefficient ring is the cone of its uniformizer power, hence site-perfect. Apply the perfect scalar projection theorem to the proper factor to obtain invertible scalar/direct comparisons on arbitrary inputs. Scalar extension commutes with tensor and pullback by their normalized balancing comparisons, and exact open scalar extension commutes with extension by zero. These give the endpoint comparisons. No constructibility or completeness of K,L is needed.

The proper counit projection scalar square follows by transposing under the geometric adjunction: both routes are the same tensor comparison followed by counit tensor identity. Use the open projection coefficient square, including the pullback compositor, for the open factor. Paste these squares to identify the reduced ordinary composite with the intrinsic finite projection through the invertible endpoint comparisons.

Apply the constant-scalar presentation of the finite proper projection. Exact realization identifies extension by zero and its unit, so its open tensor factor gives an invertible postcomposition on both sides. Pasting produces the isomorphism of arrows to the realization of the fixed-scalar finite compactification projection. This proves only identification of arrows, not projection invertibility.

proof_origin.place: Canonical-map reduction, expanded into proper scalar projection, proper/open mate squares, and constant-scalar realization.

theorem integralOrdinaryProjection_reduction_arrowComparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E]
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} (c : Compactification f)
    (aX : ProEtaleTensorModel X ((PurCompactSupport.completed l E).ring X))
    (aZ : ProEtaleTensorModel c.Z ((PurCompactSupport.completed l E).ring c.Z))
    (aY : ProEtaleTensorModel Y ((PurCompactSupport.completed l E).ring Y))
    (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E X))
    (L : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E Y)) (n : ℕ) :
    let A := Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)
    letI : Finite A := Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1) (Nat.succ_pos n)
    Nonempty (Arrow.mk ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E Y n).map
      (((PurCompactSupport.projectionMap (PurCompactSupport.completed l E) c aX aZ aY
        (PurCompactSupport.completedPull_comp l E c.i c.g)).app K).app L)) ≅
      Arrow.mk ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence Y A).functor.map
        (((ProEtale.projectionMapOfCompactification
          (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) c).app
            ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence X A).inverse.obj
              ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E X n).obj K))).app
            ((sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence Y A).inverse.obj
              ((scalarReductionDerivedExtension l E Y n).obj L)))))
